title: Mental health specialist shortage and access delays
bottleneck: Most mental health care happens in primary care, where complex or refractory cases exceed clinician expertise, while psychiatrists are scarce and concentrated in cities. Patients who fail first-line treatment face months-long waits for the specialists equipped to manage them, during which illness progresses.
why_it_blocks: Effective treatments exist for many patients, but the delivery bottleneck means they arrive late or never. Access, not pharmacology, is the binding constraint for a large share of poor outcomes.
current_state: Collaborative-care models embed psychiatry in primary care with modest success. Telepsychiatry expanded access geographically but not the absolute supply of expertise; waitlists remain long. The collaborative-care model, embedding psychiatric consultation in primary care, is the best-validated access solution, yet reimbursement rules still favor fragmented fee-for-service care.
